title: One computer for the whole organization
description:
**Phase 5 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 14f692
- **Runs in parallel with:** 6c1a9b and 0814e6 in logic, but NOT in merge order. See the warning
- **Unblocks:** 24df70, and bc830a in phase 7

---
**Scheduling warning.** This, 6c1a9b, and 0814e6 all edit models.py and messaging/store.py and will collide. Give all three to one agent or merge one at a time. This one also touches the worker protocol, so workers redeploy with it.

Computer drops user_id and is keyed by organization. computer_for_user becomes computer_for_organization; POST /computers/stopped loses user_id from its body. Update computer_affinity, shared_computer, and single_computer_start in features/.

The reason is collaboration: a shared file system is what lets a bot continue from files another bot saved, lets a person pick up what a bot left, and lets a bot finish what a person started. Handoff is the product. See docs/ORGANIZATIONS.md.

**Also update here, not before:** docs/PRODUCT.md, docs/THREAT_MODEL.md, and AGENTS.md each say user where they now say organization. They are listed under Documents this supersedes in docs/ORGANIZATIONS.md.

comments.author: home
comments.text:
**Adversarial review: what happens to a turn already running?**

Suspending an organization is now possible, and a suspended organization may have a turn in flight holding a worker lease and a computer. Decide the behavior rather than discovering it: existing turns run to completion and no new turns are accepted is the obvious answer, but silent mid-turn termination would strand a fenced computer handoff and leave the snapshot dirty.

The same question applies to the EventBridge turn-deadline scheduler and any routine wake-up, which act on behalf of an organization without a person present.
